# Setting Up Code from Previous Assignment

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(lubridate)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(baguette)
library(ranger)
library(ggplot2)

# ==========================================
# READ AND CLEAN DATA
# ==========================================

bike_data <- read_csv(
  "https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/SeoulBikeData.csv",
  locale = locale(encoding = "latin1")
)

# Check missing values
bike_data |>
  is.na() |>
  colSums()

# Check column types
attributes(bike_data)$spec

# Convert Date to date format
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  mutate(date = lubridate::dmy(Date)) |>
  select(-Date)

# Summary of variables
summary(bike_data)

# Check categorical variables
unique(bike_data$Seasons)
unique(bike_data$Holiday)
unique(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

# Convert categorical variables to factors
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  mutate(
    seasons = factor(Seasons),
    holiday = factor(Holiday),
    fn_day = factor(`Functioning Day`)
  ) |>
  select(-Seasons, -Holiday, -`Functioning Day`)

# Rename variables
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  rename(
    bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`,
    hour = Hour,
    temp = `Temperature(°C)`,
    wind_speed = `Wind speed (m/s)`,
    humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
    vis = `Visibility (10m)`,
    dew_point_temp = `Dew point temperature(°C)`,
    solar_radiation = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`,
    rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`,
    snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`
  )

# Remove non-functioning days
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  filter(fn_day == "Yes") |>
  select(-fn_day)

# Aggregate hourly data into daily observations
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  summarize(
    bike_count = sum(bike_count),
    temp = mean(temp),
    humidity = mean(humidity),
    wind_speed = mean(wind_speed),
    vis = mean(vis),
    dew_point_temp = mean(dew_point_temp),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# View cleaned data
bike_data

# ==========================================
# EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS (EDA)
# ==========================================

# Overall summary statistics for bike_count
bike_data |>
  summarize(
    across(
      bike_count,
      .fns = c(
        mean = mean,
        median = median,
        sd = sd,
        IQR = IQR,
        min = min,
        max = max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

# Summary statistics by holiday
bike_data |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      bike_count,
      .fns = c(
        mean = mean,
        median = median,
        sd = sd,
        IQR = IQR,
        min = min,
        max = max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

# Summary statistics by season
bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      bike_count,
      .fns = c(
        mean = mean,
        median = median,
        sd = sd,
        IQR = IQR,
        min = min,
        max = max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

# Summary statistics by season and holiday
bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons, holiday) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      bike_count,
      .fns = c(
        mean = mean,
        median = median,
        sd = sd,
        IQR = IQR,
        min = min,
        max = max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

# Correlation matrix for numeric variables
bike_data |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  cor() |>
  round(3)

# Bike count vs temperature
ggplot(
  bike_data,
  aes(x = temp, y = bike_count)
) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = seasons)) +
  facet_grid(~holiday)

# Bike count vs solar radiation
ggplot(
  bike_data,
  aes(x = solar_radiation, y = bike_count)
) +
  geom_point(aes(color = seasons)) +
  facet_grid(~holiday)

```

# HW 10 - Modeling Practice

```{r}
# ==========================================
# HW 10: TRAIN / TEST SPLIT
# ==========================================

library(tidymodels)

set.seed(558)

bike_split <- initial_split(
  bike_data,
  prop = 0.75,
  strata = seasons
)

bike_train <- training(bike_split)
bike_test <- testing(bike_split)

# 10-fold cross-validation on training data
set.seed(11)

bike_folds <- vfold_cv(
  bike_train,
  v = 10,
  strata = seasons
)

# Main Effects
rec1 <- recipe(bike_count ~., data = bike_train) |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow", keep_original_cols = FALSE) |>
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "Weekend", "Weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  step_rm(date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

# Recipe 2: Add Interactions
rec2 <- rec1 |>
  step_interact(
    terms = ~ starts_with("seasons_"):starts_with("holiday_") +
      starts_with("seasons_"):temp + temp:rainfall
  )

# Recipe 3: Add Quadratic Terms
rec3 <- rec2 |>
  step_mutate(
    temp_sq = temp^2,
    humidity_sq = humidity^2
  )

# Set up Linear Regression Model
lm_spec <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm")

# Create Workflows
wf1 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec1) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)

wf2 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec2) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)

wf3 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec3) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)

# Fit using 10-fold Cross-Validation
set.seed(558)

res1 <- fit_resamples(
  wf1,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

res2 <- fit_resamples(
  wf2,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

res3 <- fit_resamples(
  wf3,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# Compare Cross-Validation Results
collect_metrics(res1)
collect_metrics(res2)
collect_metrics(res3)

# Combined RMSE comparison
mlr_results <- bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(res1) |> mutate(model = "Model 1"),
  collect_metrics(res2) |> mutate(model = "Model 2"),
  collect_metrics(res3) |> mutate(model = "Model 3"),
)

mlr_results |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
```

Based on the 10-fold cross-validation results, Model 3 performed the best with the lowest RMSE of 3069.408 and MAE of 2323.075. This suggests that including the interaction and quadratic terms improves predictive performance compared with the simpler models. Model 3 was selected as the best multiple linear regression model.

## Fit the Best MLR Model using last_fit()

```{r}
# Final MLR Model: Model 3

final_mlr <- last_fit(
  wf3,
  split = bike_split,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# View test set performance
collect_metrics(final_mlr)

# Extract final fitted workflow
final_mlr_wf <- extract_workflow(final_mlr)

# View coefficient table
final_mlr_wf |>
  extract_fit_parsnip() |>
  tidy()

# View full regression summary
final_mlr_wf |>
  extract_fit_parsnip() |>
  pluck("fit") |>
  summary()
```

The final model (model 3) achieved a test RMSE of 3059.349 and MAE of 2132.168. The training R-squared was 0.9231, indicating a strong fit of the training data.

## Fit a Tuned Regression Tree

```{r}
# Regression Tree
tree_spec <- decision_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

# Create workflow using Recipe 1
tree_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec1) |>
  add_model(tree_spec)

# Create tuning grid
tree_grid <- grid_regular(
  cost_complexity(),
  tree_depth(),
  min_n(),
  levels = 3
)

# Tune using 10-fold cross-validation
set.seed(558)

tree_tune <- tune_grid(
  tree_wf,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  grid = tree_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# View tuning results
collect_metrics(tree_tune)

# Select best tree based on RMSE
best_tree <- select_best(
  tree_tune,
  metric = "rmse"
)

best_tree

# Finalize workflow with best parameters
final_tree_wf <- finalize_workflow(
  tree_wf,
  best_tree
)

# Fit final tree on entire training set
final_tree_fit <- fit(
  final_tree_wf,
  data = bike_train
)

# Plot final regression tree
final_tree_fit |>
  extract_fit_engine() |>
  rpart.plot()
  
```

```{r}
bag_spec <- bag_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart", times = 25) |>
  set_mode("regression")

# Create workflow using Recipe 1
bag_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec1) |>
  add_model(bag_spec)

# Create tuning grid
bag_grid <- grid_regular(
  cost_complexity(),
  tree_depth(),
  min_n(),
  levels = 3
)

# Tune using 10-fold cross-validation
set.seed(558)

bag_tune <- tune_grid(
  bag_wf,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  grid = bag_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# View tuning results
collect_metrics(bag_tune)

# Select best bagged tree based on RMSE
best_bag <- select_best(
  bag_tune,
  metric = "rmse"
)

best_bag

# Finalize workflow
final_bag_wf <- finalize_workflow(
  bag_wf,
  best_bag
)

# Fit best bagged tree on entire training set
final_bag_fit <- fit(
  final_bag_wf,
  data = bike_train
)
```

The bagged tree model was tuned using 10-fold cross-validation. The best tuning parameters were a cost complexity of 3.162278e-06, tree depth of 15, and minimum node size of 2. The selected model was then fitted to the entire training dataset. Its predictive performance will be evaluated on the test set and compared with the other models.

```{r}
rf_spec <- rand_forest(
  mtry = tune(),
  trees = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") |>
  set_mode("regression")

# Create workflow using Recipe 1
rf_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec1) |>
  add_model(rf_spec)

# Create a smaller tuning grid
rf_grid <- tidyr::crossing(
  mtry = c(3L, 6L, 9L),
  trees = c(100L, 300L),
  min_n = c(2L, 10L)
)

# Tune using 10-fold cross validation
set.seed(558)

rf_tune <- tune_grid(
  rf_wf,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  grid = rf_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# View tuning results
collect_metrics(rf_tune)

# Select best random forest based on RMSE
best_rf <- select_best(
  rf_tune,
  metric = "rmse"
)

best_rf

# Finalize workflow
final_rf_wf <- finalize_workflow(
  rf_wf,
  best_rf
)

# Fit best random forest on training data
final_rf_fit <- fit(
  final_rf_wf,
  data = bike_train
)
```

The random forest model was tuned using 10-fold cross-validation to select the best combination of mtry, trees, and min_n. The optimal parameters were mtry = 9, trees = 100, and min_n = 10, based on the lowest cross-validation RMSE.

The selected random forest was then fitted to the entire training dataset. Its predictive performance will be compared with the MLR, regression tree, and bagged tree models using test-set RMSE and MAE.

## Compare All Four Models on Test Set

```{r}
# Get predictions
mlr_preds <- collect_predictions(final_mlr)

tree_preds <- augment(
  final_tree_fit,
  new_data = bike_test
)

bag_preds <- augment(
  final_bag_fit,
  new_data = bike_test
)

rf_preds <- augment(
  final_rf_fit,
  new_data = bike_test
)

# Define evaluation metrics
test_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, mae)

# Calculate metrics for each model
mlr_metrics <- test_metrics(
  mlr_preds,
  truth = bike_count,
  estimate = .pred
) |>
  mutate(model = "MLR")

tree_metrics <- test_metrics(
  tree_preds,
  truth = bike_count,
  estimate = .pred
) |>
  mutate(model = "Regression Tree")

bag_metrics <- test_metrics(
  bag_preds,
  truth = bike_count,
  estimate = .pred
) |>
  mutate(model = "Bagged Tree")

rf_metrics <- test_metrics(
  rf_preds,
  truth = bike_count,
  estimate = .pred
) |>
  mutate(model = "Random Forest")

# Combine into one comparison table
final_comparison <- bind_rows(
  mlr_metrics,
  tree_metrics,
  bag_metrics,
  rf_metrics
)

final_comparison |>
  select(model, .metric, .estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = .estimate
  ) |>
  arrange(rmse)
```

## Final Model Comparison

The four models were evaluated on the test set using RMSE and MAE. The random forest performed best, with the lowest RMSE (2355.426) and MAE (1901.194), followed by the bagged tree, MLR, and regression tree. Overall, the ensemble tree methods outperformed the individual models, suggesting that combining multiple trees improves predictive accuracy for this dataset. The random forest was selected as the best overall model.

## Variable Importance Plots

```{r}
# Calculate permutation importance
perm_importance <- function(fitted_model, data) {
  predictors <- setdiff(names(data), "bike_count")
  
  baseline <- predict(fitted_model, new_data = data) |>
    bind_cols(data |> select(bike_count)) |>
    rmse(truth = bike_count, estimate = .pred) |>
    pull(.estimate)
  
  importance <- purrr::map_dfr(predictors, function(var) {
    set.seed(558)
    shuffled_data <- data
    shuffled_data[[var]] <- sample(shuffled_data[[var]])
    
    shuffled_rmse <- predict(
      fitted_model,
      new_data = shuffled_data
    ) |>
      bind_cols(data |> select(bike_count)) |>
      rmse(truth = bike_count, estimate = .pred) |>
      pull(.estimate)
    
    tibble(
      variable = var,
      importance = shuffled_rmse - baseline
    )
  })
  
  importance |> arrange(desc(importance))
}

# Bagged tree variable importance
bag_importance <- perm_importance(
  final_bag_fit,
  bike_train
)

# Random forest variable importance
rf_importance <- perm_importance(
  final_rf_fit,
  bike_train
)

# Plot bagged tree importance
ggplot(
  bag_importance,
  aes(x = reorder(variable, importance), y = importance)
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Bagged Tree Variable Importance",
    x = "Predictor",
    y = "Increase in RMSE"
  )

# Plot random forest importance
ggplot(
  rf_importance,
  aes(x = reorder(variable, importance), y = importance)
) + 
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Random Forest Variable Importance",
    x = "Predictor",
    y = "Increase in RMSE"
  )
```

## Variable Importance

The variable importance plot show that temperature and solar radiation are the most influential predictors for both the bagged tree and random forest models, followed by season and rainfall. Permuting these variables resulted in larger increases in RMSE, suggesting that they contribute substantially to predictive accuracy. Snowfall and holiday status had relatively low importance in both models.

## Fit Overall Best Model to Full Dataset

```{r}
overall_best_fit <- fit(
  final_rf_wf,
  data = bike_data
)

# Display final fitted model
overall_best_fit

# Extract fitted random forest engine
overall_best_fit |>
  extract_fit_engine()
```

Four predictive models were fitted and evaluated: multiple linear regression, regression tree, bagged tree, and random forest. Based on test-set RMSE and MAE, the random forest achieved the best predictive performance, followed by the bagged tree, MLR, and regression tree.

The random forest was selected as the overall best model based on its test-set RMSE of 2355.426 and MAE of 1901.194. The selected model was refitted using all 353 observations, with 100 trees, an mtry of 9, and a minimum node size of 10. The final model achieved an out-of-bag R-squared of approximately 0.922, indicating strong predictive performance.
